# Darkroom timeline, speed, freeze, captions, markers and export

- Kind: `editor`
- Category: `studio`
- Slug: `studio/timeline`

## Summary

How the Darkroom timeline works: tracks, splitting and trimming, ripple delete, speed changes, freeze frames, markers, captions, canvas and export formats.

## Details

Video, image, audio and LUT clips stack on separate tracks; upper video tracks cover lower ones. A clip has a timeline start, a source in/out window and a track.
Speed: 0.1× to 10×, default 1 (maintain pitch optional). A freeze frame holds one source frame; it cannot be combined with speed or reverse.
Markers: up to 500 per project, name up to 80 characters. Press M to add one at the playhead.
### Captions
Auto-captions come from Whisper (one AI job, suggested as an action); cues can be edited, styled, burned in or exported as SRT/VTT sidecars.
Caption style:
- `fontSizePct`: 1 to 15, default 4.5
- `color`: text, default "#FFFFFF"
- `backgroundColor`: text, default "#000000"
- `backgroundOpacity`: 0 to 1, default 0.55
- `position`: one of bottom, top, default "bottom"
- `maxWidthPct`: 40 to 100, default 90
### Export
Formats: h264, hevc, mp3, wav (h264/hevc render an MP4; mp3/wav are audio only). Output heights: canvas, 2160p, 1440p, 1080p, 720p. Captions: none, burn in or sidecar. Exports render on the server and count toward the plan's Darkroom export allowance.
Canvas: projects up to 4K at 24, 30 or 60 fps; vertical 9:16 for Shorts/Reels/TikTok, 1:1 and 4:5 for feeds, 16:9 for YouTube.
